title: Community pharmacy collaborative practice: written referral, consent and record formalities
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 16.03(5)(c), in accordance with 243 CMR 2.12, the collaborative practice agreement for a community pharmacy must provide that the supervising physician will: 1. provide a written referral of the patient to the authorized pharmacist; 2. specify the primary diagnosis for the patient and any secondary diagnoses in the written referral or a subsequent referral; 3. provide a copy of the written referral of the patient to the authorized pharmacist for CDTM services to the patient; and 4. obtain the patient's written informed consent to the collaboration in the collaborative practice agreement and provide a copy of the consent to the patient. Under 247 CMR 16.03(5)(d), the authorized pharmacist and supervising physician must maintain a written record of both the individual patient referral and the patient's written informed consent to the collaboration in the patient's records which are maintained by the authorized pharmacist and the supervising physician; and, in accordance with 243 CMR 2.12, the supervising physician shall maintain the original patient consent to the referral in the record in the custody of the supervising physician, transmit a copy of the patient's consent to the authorized pharmacist within 24 hours, and provide copies of the referral and consent to the patient in a timely manner. Under 247 CMR 16.04(1), in the community pharmacy setting the CDTM agreement shall include (a) a written referral of a specific patient from the supervising physician to an authorized pharmacist and (b) the written consent of the patient to the CDTM agreement. 243 CMR 2.12(4)(e)3. and 5. state the referral, consent and record items in substantially the same words, 243 CMR 2.12(1) states that in the community pharmacy setting the CDTM agreement shall include a written referral of an identified patient and a written consent to the CDTM agreement by the named patient, and 243 CMR 2.12(4)(e)4. adds that the patient's written consent form shall include the statement: "The pharmacist shall not replace the physician as the principal medical decision maker."
exam_relevance: Tests the community pharmacy paperwork: what the agreement must require the supervising physician to do about the referral and consent, who keeps which record, the 24-hour transmission of the consent copy, and the statement the Board of Registration in Medicine requires in the consent form.

authority.name: Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations
Board of Registration in Medicine regulations
authority.section: 243 CMR 2.12(1), definition of CDTM agreement; 243 CMR 2.12(4)(e)3., 4. and 5.

numeric_facts.fact: Time for the supervising physician to transmit a copy of the patient's consent to the authorized pharmacist

common_confusions: The referral and consent duties in 247 CMR 16.03(5)(c) are duties the agreement must provide that the supervising physician will perform, not duties placed on the pharmacist.

The written record of referral and consent is maintained by both the authorized pharmacist and the supervising physician, while the original consent stays in the record in the supervising physician's custody.

The 24-hour period runs to the supervising physician's transmission of a copy of the patient's consent to the authorized pharmacist; copies of the referral and consent go to the patient in a timely manner, with no hour count stated.
Secondary diagnoses may be specified in the written referral or in a subsequent referral.
The consent-form statement that the pharmacist shall not replace the physician as the principal medical decision maker appears in 243 CMR 2.12(4)(e)4.; 247 CMR 16.03(5) does not state it.
verification_notes: Read in the current mass.gov PDF of 247 CMR 16.00 (regulation page dated 12/15/2017) and in the current mass.gov PDF of 243 CMR 2.00 on 2026-09-17.
